key_insight: Flutter onset in this pitching finite wing is governed by where aerodynamic energy is transferred, with the leading edge switching from damping to the main source of excitation near the stability boundary.
engineering_relevance: Controlling the leading-edge flow and pressure evolution offers a direct path to suppress low-Re flutter in finite wings and similar lifting surfaces.
method: Direct numerical simulations of incompressible flow over an aspect-ratio-two NACA 0015 wing at Re = 1000
Lobe-resolved force-moment partitioning to localize vortical contributions to aeroelastic power
Comparison across fixed-speed, slowly growing-amplitude, free-pitching, and forced-response cases
evidence_signal: The net aerodynamic work changes sign near U* = 4.25, with leading-edge positive work nearly balanced by trailing-edge negative work near onset and confirmed by both free-pitching and matched forced-response calculations.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on a specific low-Re, aspect-ratio-two wing model and may not transfer directly to higher-Reynolds-number or different-geometry flutter systems without revalidation.
paper_title: Leading-edge energy transfer governs flutter onset of a pitching finite wing in low-Reynolds number flows
